verbatim.basis: Snippet 'Monolayer cultures containing Potaba showed a dose-dependent inhibition... similar dose dependent inhibition of glycosaminoglycan secretion in all 3 groups' is present verbatim in the abstract read independently via PubMed (Acta Dermato-Venereol, 1992).

subject_grounding.basis: The study used 'Potaba' = potassium para-aminobenzoate, the potassium SALT, whereas edge subject MESH:D010129 is the free acid 'aminobenzoic acid' (4-aminobenzoic acid/PABA). Same active anion but the cited entity is the salt form, not the MeSH-grounded free acid.

object_grounding.basis: Abstract explicitly says 'glycosaminoglycan secretion', matching object MESH:D006025 Glycosaminoglycans.

polarity.basis: 'dose-dependent inhibition of glycosaminoglycan secretion' = decrease, matches 'decreases abundance of'.

direction.basis: The drug (Potaba) is the agent inhibiting GAG secretion by fibroblasts; subject acts on object.

granularity.basis: 'GAG secretion' is a production/abundance readout; abstract notes it is 'a direct effect of the drug rather than an indirect effect of changes in cell density' — consistent with decreasing abundance.

scope_modality.basis: In-vitro fibroblast lines from lichen sclerosus, morphoea, and normal skin — NOT dermatomyositis (the disease in path_context). Effect is asserted at 10-1,000 ug/ml; therapeutic relevance is only 'suggested' as a 'possible target'. Narrow context over-generalized to the path's disease.

source_type.basis: In-vitro fibroblast monolayer culture study → IN_VITRO.

independent_grounding.source: PubMed abstract read in memory (PMID:1350132), plus ChEMBL mechanism lookup for aminobenzoic acid (CHEMBL542)
independent_grounding.record: Abstract confirms Potaba dose-dependently inhibits GAG secretion in dermal fibroblast lines; ChEMBL has NO curated mechanism record for aminobenzoic acid, so no independent target/action grounding available.

verdicts.note: Snippet is genuine and on-topic for the GAG-decrease relation. Two gaps: (1) the tested agent is the potassium salt, not the free-acid MeSH entity; (2) the cell models are scleroderma-spectrum sclerosing conditions, not dermatomyositis. The active moiety is the same p-aminobenzoate, so edge is defensible, but the citation's subject is the salt and its context is a different disease.
verdicts.issue_for_curator: The cited experiment tests the potassium SALT of the subject drug, not the free-acid form named by the edge subject; and the cells studied are from sclerosing skin conditions, not the disease named later in the path. Confirm the effect for the subject drug's own grounded form and, ideally, in a context relevant to the path's disease.

Acid mucopolysaccharide secretion by rheumatoid synovial cells and scleroderma fibroblasts was inhibited even at 100 microgram/ml' is present verbatim in the abstract (J Invest Dermatol, 1979).

object_grounding.basis: 'Acid mucopolysaccharide' is the historical synonym for glycosaminoglycan; matches object MESH:D006025.

polarity.basis: 'secretion... was inhibited even at 100 microgram/ml' and 'over 50% inhibition at 5000 microgram/ml' = decrease, matches predicate.

direction.basis: Drug inhibits mucopolysaccharide secretion by cells; subject acts on object.

granularity.basis: Secretion/synthesis readout consistent with decreasing abundance.

scope_modality.basis: Cell types are scleroderma fibroblasts and rheumatoid synovial cells — NOT dermatomyositis. Effect stated as within therapeutic range at 100 ug/ml, but disease context differs from the path.

source_type.basis: In-vitro fibroblast/synovial cell culture study → IN_VITRO.

independent_grounding.source: PubMed abstract read in memory (PMID:155125); ChEMBL mechanism lookup (CHEMBL542)
independent_grounding.record: Abstract confirms potassium para-aminobenzoate inhibits acid mucopolysaccharide (GAG) secretion by scleroderma fibroblasts and rheumatoid synovial cells within therapeutic range. ChEMBL has no curated mechanism for aminobenzoic acid.

verdicts.note: Solid GAG-decrease evidence, but again the tested entity is the salt and the disease context is scleroderma/RA, not dermatomyositis. Two independent studies converge on the same relation, strengthening edge_supported even though each citation's subject is the salt form.
verdicts.issue_for_curator: The tested agent is the potassium salt of the subject drug rather than the free-acid form named by the edge; and the model systems are from scleroderma/rheumatoid tissue, not the disease named in the path. The GAG-lowering relation is corroborated, but the subject-form and disease-context mismatch should be addressed.

verdict.edge_basis: Two independent in-vitro studies (read directly from PubMed, both concordant) show potassium para-aminobenzoate — sharing the same active p-aminobenzoate moiety as the free acid MESH:D010129 — dose-dependently inhibits glycosaminoglycan/acid-mucopolysaccharide secretion by dermal fibroblasts, establishing the decreases-abundance relation. Caveats: (1) no ChEMBL curated mechanism exists to independently ground the drug's action, and (2) the cited studies use the salt form and scleroderma/lichen-sclerosus/rheumatoid models rather than the free acid and dermatomyositis; the relation is real but the citations under-specify the exact subject form and disease context.

verbatim.basis: Abstract BACKGROUND contains verbatim: 'Dermal mucin is an amorphous gelatinous substance composed primarily of hyaluronan (HA) and sulphated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)' and 'deposition is associated with lupus erythematosus, dermatomyositis, scleroderma and granuloma annulare.'

subject_grounding.basis: Snippet is explicitly about sulphated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), matching subject MESH:D006025 Glycosaminoglycans; dermal mucin is defined as composed of HA + sulphated GAGs.

object_grounding.basis: Snippet names dermatomyositis (MESH:D003882) explicitly as a disorder with which mucin/GAG deposition is associated.

polarity.basis: 'manifestation of' is a presence/finding relation; the source states GAG (mucin) deposition IS a finding associated with dermatomyositis — positive presence, consistent with the predicate.

direction.basis: GAG deposition is presented as a finding/consequence within dermatomyositis (deposition associated with the disease), i.e. GAG deposition is a manifestation of the disease, not vice versa.

granularity.basis: The finding is specifically dermal DEPOSITION of GAGs (mucinosis), not GAGs as a free chemical. The edge subject 'Glycosaminoglycans' abstracts away the deposition/localization, but the source clearly ties the manifestation to GAG accumulation.

scope_modality.basis: Stated as an established association in a review-style background ('mucin deposition is an additional finding, and deposition is associated with... dermatomyositis'), not hedged as hypothesis; a caveat is that 'the underlying cause... is unknown' — but the manifestation itself is asserted.

source_type.basis: British Journal of Dermatology clinical/laboratory study with review background; evidence_source is clinical/observational literature (OTHER acceptable).

independent_grounding.record: Dermatomyositis panniculitis series: 'abundant mucin interstitially deposited between collagen bundles of the dermis were also frequent findings' — confirms GAG/mucin deposition is a histopathologic manifestation of dermatomyositis.

verdicts.note: Verbatim, correct entities, correct direction. Only a minor granularity abstraction (GAG chemical vs GAG deposition/mucinosis). Independent source PMID:29524269 corroborates the manifestation.

subject_grounding.basis: Snippet explicitly names 'deposition of glycosaminoglycans (mucin)', matching subject MESH:D006025 Glycosaminoglycans.

polarity.basis: Positive-presence relation: dermal mucinosis (GAG deposition) occurs secondary to dermatomyositis, consistent with 'manifestation of'.

direction.basis: 'secondary to... dermatomyositis' establishes GAG deposition as downstream/consequent to the disease, i.e. a manifestation of it — correct direction.

source_type.basis: American Journal of Dermatopathology clinicopathologic report/background; observational clinical literature (OTHER).

independent_grounding.record: Confirms mucin (GAG) deposition in the dermis is a frequent finding in dermatomyositis, corroborating the secondary-mucinosis association stated here.

verdicts.note: Verbatim, correct entities and direction; same minor granularity abstraction as the other citation. Well corroborated.

verdict.edge_basis: Independent source PMID:29524269 (dermatomyositis panniculitis series, not cited by the curator) explicitly reports 'abundant mucin interstitially deposited between collagen bundles of the dermis' as a frequent finding in dermatomyositis; mucin is composed of glycosaminoglycans. This, plus the two cited dermatopathology sources, establishes GAG (mucin) deposition as a recognized cutaneous manifestation of dermatomyositis. The only soft spot is granularity — the manifestation is dermal deposition of GAGs (mucinosis), which the edge abstracts to the GAG chemical entity itself — but this is within acceptable DrugMechDB abstraction and does not invalidate the edge.
